compatibility.governance: Neither profile nor reader policy attests authority, provenance, creation time, currentness, permission, or publication status.
compatibility.historical: All .2 tag-bearing bytes continue to decode under current selected tag rules. The bytes do not attest which Python object produced them. Preserve exact originals; any source-qualified migration is a new artifact/view with lineage and actual time.
compatibility.option_a: Reader-first .3 rollout; writer enablement only after installed/no-checkout consumers verify; rollback disables writers first and retains readers for emitted .3 artifacts.
compatibility.option_b: Keep .2 wire law and readers; enforce early API admission with typed refusal and no store/cache side effects.

automatic CAS rewrite/readdressing or profileless mapping import
decision_request.option_a: Add a .3.0 mapping escape in the existing canonical owner(s), patterned on runner mapping/entries. Readers first; preserve .2 readers and bytes. Keep every other Core/IR tag policy separate. Invalidate or generation-separate old in-memory Foundry specialization cache entries across rollout. Never infer .2 producer intent or rewrite CAS.
decision_request.option_a_cache_requirement: Version or generation-separate Foundry specialization keys/cache entries across rollout; the current equality hash has a raw-map/native-value predecessor collision.
decision_request.option_a_producer_requirement: The new mapping envelope must not be asked to recover input type after a producer converted both raw Mapping and Decimal/bytes/float to plain dictionaries. Update Foundry's converter to retain native values or an explicit internal typed carrier.
decision_request.option_b: Document and validate reserved-map refusal at run_experiment, direct state/checkpoint/cache persistence, and Foundry static params before conversion/lookup; propagate typed refusal past the broad exception fallback. No profile bump, but public API domain narrows.
decision_request.question: Should ordinary mappings containing literal _type be a losslessly representable value in persisted canonical artifacts and Foundry static-cache keys, or should accepted runtime inputs be narrowed under .2 before persistence/cache lookup?

Current compute_static_params_hash returns the same hash 98ca27689bf22ddf3b430fe7c242ad16 for raw nested mapping and Decimal.
JSON mode keeps raw map as object and emits Decimal as string '1'; projections differ. This falsifies applying the collision to state_read_projection.

selected_law.binding: Core and IR share mechanics but keep strict owner-specific tag policies; no universal registry or decoder fallback; Core array_digest acceptance and IR refusal are compatible; a future universal value grammar needs a separately versioned semantic contract and migration; profile declaration is not producer attestation.

_type is reserved for canonical typed envelopes; unknown tags refuse; ordinary mappings preserve explicit None. This does not add a validator to ExperimentState's unrestricted dict[str, Any] admission.

Historical reads preserve source semantics; no auto-conversion or blanket grandfathering; any persisted migration is a new artifact/view with lineage and actual time; readers-first rollout and writer-first rollback.
